clinicalPearls: A fulminant systemic neoplasm of natural killer cells, more common in East Asian populations and typically affecting younger to middle-aged adults
Presents acutely with fever, marked hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, and rapid clinical deterioration, often with a leukaemic blood and marrow picture
Almost always associated with Epstein-Barr virus, with detectable circulating viral DNA
Neoplastic cells express CD56 and cytoplasmic CD3-epsilon while lacking surface CD3, with cytotoxic molecules and frequent EBV-encoded RNA positivity
Haemophagocytic syndrome, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and multi-organ failure frequently complicate the course
Overlaps biologically with extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type, but differs in its leukaemic, disseminated presentation
Prompt recognition is critical given the extremely rapid clinical trajectory
reference.pathophysiology: Aggressive NK-cell leukaemia is a highly aggressive systemic proliferation of Epstein-Barr virus-infected natural killer cells. Latent EBV within the neoplastic NK cells contributes to transformation, and the malignant cells disseminate through blood, bone marrow, liver, and spleen. Massive cytokine release and cytotoxic activity commonly trigger a haemophagocytic syndrome and coagulopathy, driving rapid multi-organ dysfunction. The disease shares viral and immunophenotypic features with extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma but is distinguished by its leukaemic dissemination and explosive course.
additionalDifferentials: Extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, nasal type, with dissemination
Chronic lymphoproliferative disorder of NK cells (an indolent entity)
Aggressive T-cell leukaemias or lymphomas with leukaemic spread
additionalInvestigations: Peripheral blood film and bone marrow examination with immunophenotyping
Flow cytometry showing CD56 positivity and surface CD3 negativity with cytoplasmic CD3-epsilon
In situ hybridisation for EBV-encoded RNA and plasma EBV DNA quantification
Coagulation screen and markers of disseminated intravascular coagulation
Ferritin, triglycerides, and fibrinogen to assess for haemophagocytic syndrome
Cross-sectional imaging of liver and spleen and biochemical organ-function assessment
redFlags: Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis with worsening cytopenias and hyperferritinaemia
reference.prognosis: The prognosis is extremely poor with survival often measured in weeks to a few months; intensive asparaginase-containing chemotherapy followed by allogeneic stem-cell transplantation offers the only prospect of durable control in fit patients.
pitfalls: Mistaking the presentation for reactive EBV-driven haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis and delaying oncological treatment
Overlooking surface CD3 negativity that distinguishes NK from T-cell disease
Using anthracycline-based regimens that are relatively ineffective owing to drug efflux
references: Swerdlow SH et al. WHO monograph on lymphoid neoplasms
management: ANKL is a fulminant, EBV-driven systemic NK-cell proliferation; treatment intent is disease control with an attempt at cure via transplant, with no watch-and-wait option
First line is intensive asparaginase-containing chemotherapy, used because ANKL cells characteristically resist conventional anthracycline-based regimens
Second-line/relapsed disease has no well-established standard regimen; manage individually in consultation with a haemato-oncology/transplant centre
Surgery has no role since ANKL is a systemic leukaemic disease, not a localized mass
Radiotherapy is not part of standard ANKL management; the RT-based approach used for localized nasal-type extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma should not be extrapolated to ANKL
Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation should be offered to fit patients who respond to induction chemotherapy, as it is the only realistic prospect of durable disease control

Haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis frequently complicates ANKL and should be treated as an oncologic emergency with immunosuppressive and cytotoxic therapy plus organ support, run in parallel with disease-directed chemotherapy
Disseminated intravascular coagulation is corrected with fresh frozen plasma, cryoprecipitate, and platelet transfusion as needed
Broad supportive care is required from presentation, including transfusion support, tumour lysis syndrome prophylaxis, and antimicrobial prophylaxis given profound immune compromise
Plasma EBV DNA is tracked serially as a marker of disease activity and response
Ferritin, triglycerides, and fibrinogen are followed to detect and monitor haemophagocytic activity, alongside coagulation parameters, cytopenias, and hepatic/organ function
Refer emergently at the point of suspicion or diagnosis to a transplant-capable haemato-oncology unit, without delaying for staging completeness
Involve palliative care early and in parallel with disease-directed treatment given the very poor prognosis, so goals-of-care discussions happen alongside rather than after treatment
